summary: Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under K. L. Dhammajoti and also studied under Bhante Dhammasakkaro.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who earned her BA from the University of Cambridge. She held positions at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, and King's College London, before becoming George A. Saden Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale in 2006.

Verrier Elwin was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Dean Close School and Merton College. From circa 1946 to 1949, he served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

Vesna Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley. She held positions at Berkeley, served as Numata Chair at Oxford through 2010, and was a professor at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2007–2014).

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale and a PhD from SOAS University of London. In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History and Professor of Asian and Comparative History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who studied as a graduate student at the University of Chicago. In 2005, he founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education and served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. In 2007, he was attested as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Dartmouth, the University of Washington, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD circa 1976), he taught at Harvard and joined the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Victor Henry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Douai, École Centrale de Lille, and the University of Lille, before becoming professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris in 1888.

Victor Turner was an anthropologist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from UCL and the University of Manchester. He held appointments at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell, the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).
Victoria Sujata is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Michael Aris and earned her PhD from Harvard University.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was an Indian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a pandit, supervisor of collation, and principal at Visva-Bharati University, and later as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Cambridge. She taught at Sydney, Hong Kong, and SPA Delhi, worked at the Smithsonian, and became Barbara Stoler Miller Professor of Indian Art at Columbia in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (ca. 1968–1989), Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (ca. 1984–1987), and held visiting professorships in California and Washington.
Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijayadharma Suri (attested 1933) and founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist and scholar of Central Asian studies who earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen. He spent his career there as Privatdozent, associate professor, and professor (1887–1913), and became President of the Royal Danish Academy in 1909.

Vimla Karnatak is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar. As attested in 2000, she served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University.

Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist who studied at the University of Prague under Moriz Winternitz and Josef Zubatý between 1903 and 1909. He later held a post at Charles University's Faculty of Arts from circa 1924 to 1953.

Vincent Arthur Smith was a historian and Indologist educated at Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1871 to 1900 and later worked at the University of Oxford and as Curator of the Indian Institute (circa 1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lucia Dolce, earned his MA and PhD from Leiden University with additional studies at Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono universities, and was attested as a research fellow at Leiden in 2012.
